title: The finite field with $q$ elements
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and put $q=p^a$. A *finite field with $q$ elements* is a field $F$ whose underlying set is finite of cardinality $q$. Such a field exists (for instance the splitting field of $X^{q}-X$ over the prime field $\mathbf F_p=\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z$), it has characteristic $p$, and any two fields with $q$ elements are isomorphic; $\mathbf F_q$ denotes one fixed such field. Conversely every finite field has $p^f$ elements, where $p$ is its characteristic and $f\geq1$.
